question: When trained only for next-token prediction on controlled stochastic processes, do neural activations linearly encode the minimal predictive-belief geometry even when the smallest finite generator is quantum or post-quantum rather than a finite classical HMM?

key_findings.claim: Transformer and recurrent-network activations admit low-error affine maps to the exact predictive states of classical, one-qubit, and post-quantum process generators.
key_findings.evidence: The authors generate sequences from Mess3, BlochWalk, and Moon processes, concatenate last-token activations across layers, and fit weighted affine probes to exact Bayesian-filter states. Trained Transformer and LSTM projections reproduce the simplex fractal, Bloch-disk slice, and curved GPT manifold, whereas identically probed random networks do not.

anchors.section: IV Neural Networks Discover Minimal Belief Geometries

key_findings.claim: For the quantum and post-quantum processes, learned representations fit the low-dimensional generalized generator better than a Markov-order-3 classical approximation.
key_findings.evidence: The finite classical comparison is chosen to have dimensionality comparable to model hidden states, yet its affine-probe RMSE remains high while the exact generalized generator fits well. During BlochWalk training, normalized RMSE to the quantum target falls by more than 80% in roughly 20-40 epochs while the classical-approximation fit remains poor.

key_findings.claim: The recovered geometry preserves pairwise relationships rather than only allowing independent state decoding.
key_findings.evidence: Across the three main processes and Transformer/LSTM models, cosine similarities between pairs of recovered beliefs and the exact minimal geometry have R-squared between 0.99 and 1.00. Fits to classical approximations range roughly from 0.36 to 0.88, depending on process and architecture.

key_findings.claim: The phenomenon recurs across Transformer, LSTM, vanilla RNN, and GRU variants, but the experiments establish finite-precision representational equivalence rather than a physical quantum speedup.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix figures repeat the probe comparison across four architectures and hyperparameter sweeps. The discussion stresses that a d-dimensional Hilbert-space mixed state may require d^2 real coordinates in a classical network, so compositional quantum state spaces still scale exponentially and ordinary neural networks do not replace large quantum circuits.

method.core_idea: Use stochastic processes whose minimal classical, quantum, or generalized-probabilistic generators are known exactly, then test whether trained sequence-model activations are an affine coordinate system for their predictive states.
method.mechanism: Generalized hidden Markov models express word probabilities and history-conditioned future distributions through linear transition operators. Exact Bayesian filtering produces a canonical predictive-state geometry. Networks receive only token sequences and next-token loss; weighted least-squares probes map concatenated hidden activations to exact belief vectors, with random-network, finite-order classical, architecture, layer, and training-time comparisons.
assumptions: Affine decodability is meaningful evidence that a model internally represents the target belief coordinates.
The supplied GHMMs are minimal or have known finite-dimensional impossibility results for the competing physical model classes.
Synthetic stationary ergodic processes are informative model organisms for learned predictive state.
Finite floating-point continuous activations may emulate generalized state vectors without implementing quantum physics.

techniques.role: Provides one linear formalism spanning classical, quantum, and post-quantum finite-memory generators.
Computes the history-indexed target representation over all possible futures.
Tests whether hidden activations linearly recover exact predictive coordinates while weighting histories by occurrence probability.
Compares the target with a finite classical approximation of comparable dimension.
Checks pairwise cosine relationships, not just pointwise probe error.
Tracks when the representation appears relative to validation loss and depth.

evaluations.setting: Mess3, BlochWalk, and Moon stochastic processes
evaluations.metric: Weighted affine-probe RMSE to exact generator beliefs
evaluations.result: Trained Transformer and LSTM activations closely reproduce each minimal belief manifold and outperform Markov-order-3 and random-network comparisons.
evaluations.baseline: Random initialization and finite classical Markov approximation

evaluations.setting: Pairwise belief geometry across three processes and two architectures
evaluations.result: Exact minimal representations attain 0.99-1.00; classical comparisons are substantially lower, approximately 0.36-0.88.
evaluations.baseline: Pairwise geometry of the classical finite-order approximation

evaluations.setting: BlochWalk over training time and network depth
evaluations.result: Quantum-target error drops by more than 80% during early training and generally improves in later layers and concatenated representations.
Transformer, LSTM, GRU, and vanilla RNN variants show the same qualitative preference for the minimal geometry.

limitations: All data-generating processes are small synthetic systems with exactly known latent structure, not natural language or frontier-scale models.
A learned affine probe demonstrates accessible information but does not prove the network causally uses the decoded coordinates in the claimed update algorithm.
The classical comparison is a selected Markov-order-3 approximation rather than an exhaustive finite-precision classical representation search.
Terms such as quantum and post-quantum describe geometry and memory realization classes; the trained networks remain classical numerical systems.
Architecture universality is empirical over a finite set of small networks and hyperparameters.
The experiments do not intervene on or patch the proposed belief coordinates to measure prediction changes.
failure_modes: A high-capacity activation space supports an affine decoder for many correlated targets without using the target representation computationally.
Probe fitting on overlapping or probability-weighted histories hides errors on rare, long, or extrapolative contexts.
A nonminimal or incorrectly specified generator makes the apparent preference for exotic geometry an artifact of target coordinates.
Finite precision turns a formal infinite-state separation into an approximation whose memory advantage depends on the error tolerance.
Concatenating all layers can conceal that no individual model state carries a dynamically closed belief representation.
reusable_insights: Design interpretability benchmarks around processes with exact minimal predictive states and falsifiable geometry.
Compare a decoded representation with realistic alternative coordinate systems, not only a random-probe baseline.
Audit relational geometry and update dynamics in addition to pointwise linear decodability.
Track representation formation during training to distinguish learned structure from architectural priors.
Keep representational compression claims separate from physical-computation and runtime-advantage claims.
open_questions: Do causal interventions along decoded belief axes produce the exact predicted next-token changes?
Can the geometry be recovered from a single recurrently sufficient layer rather than a concatenation across depth?
How does approximation error scale with context length, rare histories, precision, and generator dimension?
Do natural-language models contain local subspaces corresponding to identifiable generalized predictive-state models?
Which architecture-dependent algorithms implement the same architecture-independent belief geometry?
Does belief-geometry fidelity predict out-of-distribution sequence generalization?

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
competitive_landscape.difference: Shai et al. establish linear belief-state geometry for classical hidden-state processes in Transformers; the reviewed paper extends the target class to quantum and post-quantum minimal generators and broadens the architecture sweep.

competitive_landscape.title: Constrained belief updates explain geometric structures in transformer representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Piotrowski et al. derive attention, OV, and embedding mechanisms as architecture-constrained Bayesian updates in classical HMM tasks; the reviewed work has broader generator physics and architecture invariance but a less causal circuit-level account.

competitive_landscape.title: Quantum theory in finite dimension cannot explain every general process with finite memory
competitive_landscape.difference: Fanizza et al. prove and construct the post-quantum finite-memory separation that supplies the Moon process; the reviewed paper asks whether ordinary learned continuous representations recover that geometry from observations.

competitive_landscape.title: Next-token pretraining implies in-context learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Riechers et al. connect next-token pretraining and in-context inference more generally; the reviewed experiment focuses on exact low-dimensional belief manifolds and representation-class separations rather than task adaptation.

novelty_assessment: The core extension—probing learned predictive geometry for processes with finite quantum but no finite classical generator, and finite generalized but no finite quantum generator—is distinctive and cleanly grounded in prior realization theorems. The evidence strongly supports affine accessibility and cross-architecture recurrence on controlled systems, but causal use, natural-data relevance, and the rhetoric of intrinsic discovery remain less established than geometric probe fit.
reviewer_notes: Read the 30-page extracted manuscript, including the GHMM formalism, main figures, architecture appendices, training details, and the authors' quantum-advantage qualification. Competitor and foundation papers were checked at their primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23. Claims use 'nominally quantum' for representation class and do not attribute physical quantum computation to the networks.
